title: POC scoping - Private networking & data residency - Aurora HealthTech
summary: POC scoping to validate private networking options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), region/data residency, and benchmark goals. Agreement on 2-week benchmark window, success criteria (p95 latency < 250ms for text-gen, sustained 120 QPS with batching), and next steps to exchange security docs and schedule VPC peering dry-run.
topics: regional data residency and egress constraints
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we appreciate the time. quick intros - I'm Maya Chen, AE on the account.
[00:10] Lena: Hi Maya, Lena here head of infra at Aurora, thanks. Mark, Priya and Tom from our side.
[00:18] Samir: Samir Patel, Redwood solutions engineer - I'll lead the technical scoping.
[00:25] Mark: great, quick agenda from our side: networking constraints, compliance questions, and then benchmark sizing.
[00:35] Maya: perfect. So quick context: Aurora wants private deployment with strict data residency in eu-west-1 and us-east-1, egress restrictions to only specific IP ranges, and you want to run a POC to validate perf and costs. correct?
[00:48] Lena: yes, and we need to know if VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink is better for our topology - we can't open inbound internet from our EHR cluster.
[00:58] Samir: totally. Quick clarification: when you say "private deployment" are you leaning to Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC) or Redwood Dedicated inside our tenancy?
[01:08] Mark: we want customer-managed networking, so VPC-to-VPC peering or PrivateLink into Redwood's control plane. we can't have data leave region or go via public internet.
[01:20] Priya: also need audit logs and KMS integration for keys; SOC2/ISO type evidence as well.
[01:28] Maya: understood. We'll share SOC2 and the security pack after this call. For the networking tradeoffs: VPC peering is straightforward and lower-latency but requires route table and cross-account peering; PrivateLink (iface endpoints) gives more controlled egress and is easier for cross-account access and for restricting traffic to specific subnets. Samir do you want to add?
[01:50] Samir: yeah, and operationally PrivateLink lets you avoid transitive routing issues; peering is fine but if you have multiple VPCs you'd end up managing many peering connections. Also note PrivateLink has ENI limits and costs per hour per endpoint.
[02:05] Tom: ENI limits - is that per AZ? we operate large clusters in three AZs.
[02:12] Samir: yes per AZ per region; we can size endpoints and we can work with you to ensure quotas are raised. For throughput, PrivateLink can do multiple Gbps, for our typical inference it's fine. The other thing is egress constraints - if you must egress only to specific on-prem ranges we can configure NAT/Transit Gateway routes but that tends to add latency.
[02:34] Lena: on region residency - we want data stored and processed only in eu-west-1 for EU patients. Are we able to pin a model instance to a region?
[02:43] Maya: yes you can pin model variants to run in specific regions under Redwood Private. We'll ensure the model weights and inference happen in your chosen region. we'll provide data residency guarantee language for the SOW.
[02:56] Mark: for the POC success criteria: we want p95 latency under 250ms for short prompts (~50 tokens) and sustained 120 QPS during peak with batching enabled. is that realistic?
[03:08] Samir: 250ms p95 is tight but doable for smaller models or optimized kernels; for larger 70B style models p95 will be higher. We should scope model family - do you plan to use a 13B or 70B-ish model?
[03:22] Nina: our initial plan is to test a smaller generation model for chat-like triage, so 13B family to start. If that passes we'll test larger models for complex summarization.
[03:32] Samir: great. For 13B with proper batching and KV cache and sequence lengths of ~64 tokens, 120 QPS is achievable with a small dedicated pool. We need to know tokens per request and average sequence length to give exact sizing.
[03:45] Mark: avg prompt ~60 tokens, response ~120 tokens. daily load expected ~80k requests per day with spikes to 200k during batch jobs.
[03:56] Samir: helpful. We'll translate that to concurrency and GPU counts; initial estimate: for 13B quantized profile you'd likely need 3-4 GPUs for the steady 120 QPS with batching and 1-2 additional GPUs for headroom during spikes. We'll run a bench to validate.
[04:12] Priya: security wise we need KMS integration and customer-managed keys. also RBAC and SSO (SAML) for console access.
[04:22] Maya: we support SAML SSO and we can integrate with your IdP. KMS integration is supported; we'll send the options (KMS/HSM) in the security pack.
[04:31] Mark: about egress - we must prevent tokenized data from leaving eu-west-1. Does Redwood Private allow us to block any egress outside region?
[04:40] Samir: yes you can configure routing to keep traffic in region. we'll also ensure the control plane communication for metrics can go over your private link - we can offer a private control plane option. There might be additional configuration in the SOW for metrics shipping.
[04:54] Lena: ok. Let's talk bench plan - timeline and what we'll run.
[05:00] Samir: propose a two-week bench window: week 1 baseline functional and connectivity (VPC peering/PrivateLink setup, KMS, SSO). Week 2 load testing across representative prompts: 50-token, 200-token, and a long summarization 1k-token test. We'll run steady QPS runs and spike tests, record p50/p95/p99, and measure token/sec cost.
[05:20] Nina: who from Redwood sets up the peering? we need an AWS account owner from your side.
[05:25] Maya: we'll assign a deployment engineer - I'll loop in Rajiv for VPC peering coordination. he'll handle cross-account role and endpoint creation.
[05:33] Tom: for the bench can we run our own synthetic generator? we prefer using our traffic shape and also replay some production traces (sanitized).
[05:40] Samir: absolutely, we can accept replayed traces - please sanitize PHI. We'll provide a benchmarking harness and a lightweight agent you can run from your VPC to simulate traffic.
[05:50] Mark: any constraints about TLS or mutual TLS? we require mTLS for control plane APIs.
[05:57] Samir: we support TLS; mTLS for control plane is available in Private deployments - we'll confirm the exact API surface and cert exchange process in the security docs.
[06:08] Priya: also need audit logs shipped to our SIEM, retention for 7 years for compliance.
[06:15] Maya: we can stream audit logs to your S3 bucket or to a SIEM via our log forwarder; retention and export are supported.
[06:23] Mark: great. Let's name the explicit success criteria so we all agree.
[06:28] Samir: proposal: 1) connectivity: PrivateLink or VPC peering established and test traffic passes. 2) Residency: all inference and ephemeral state kept in eu-west-1 for EU data. 3) Perf: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (50 tokens) and sustained 120 QPS for 13B with acceptable cost per token. 4) Security: KMS integration, SAML SSO, audit log delivery verified. 5) Stability: no more than 1% error rate during bench window.
[07:02] Nina: that looks good. what's the expected time to stand up the network in our AWS accounts?
[07:08] Samir: typically 2-3 business days to create endpoints and tests if quotas are in place. if you need quota increases that can add time - request them early.
[07:18] Lena: quotas are often the blocker. we'll start quota requests today.
[07:22] Maya: timeline-wise: we can kick off next Monday. Week 1 networking and small functional tests; week 2 heavy bench. Deliverable is a bench report and cost estimate.
[07:33] Mark: about cost - do you have an estimate for 3-4 GPUs for the steady state and the bench?
[07:40] Samir: rough hosted equivalent cost for the bench would be X/hr per GPU - (note: Samir mumbles a number) but since this is Private we'll give you a dedicated quote; during the POC we can provide temporary discounted capacity for validation. We'll follow up via pricing sheet.
[07:58] Priya: are there any vendor lock-in concerns? if we need to move later how hard is it?
[08:05] Maya: models and prompts are portable; runtime configs and quantization profiles are documented. We provide exportable logs and model versioning data so migration is possible. We'll include that in the SOW.
[08:18] Tom: network topology question: our EHR VPC does not have NAT; outbound allowed only to specific services. For PrivateLink we'll need interface endpoints and route them through private subnets. Does Redwood support endpoint service names that we can reference?
[08:33] Samir: yes we'll create an AWS Endpoint Service (com.amazonaws.us-east-1.vpce-svc-xxxx) you can accept and attach to specific subnets; we'll coordinate the acceptance flow.
[08:45] Lena: perfect. can you share a diagram of the expected routing?
[08:49] Maya: yes we'll attach a sample topology diagram in the follow-up email.
[08:53] Mark: on monitoring - we need token-level billing and per-route latency breakdowns. is that available in Private?
[08:59] Samir: yes Redwood Console can be configured in Private to show token-level cost, per-route dashboards, traces. we'll show you a demo or share screenshots.
[09:09] Nina: ok next steps recap would be helpful.
[09:12] Maya: absolutely. I'll recap: 1) Maya to send security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS options) and a sample SOW by Tue 2026-12-07. 2) Rajiv (deployment eng) to coordinate VPC peering/PrivateLink and share endpoint service name - target by Thu 2026-12-10. 3) Customer to request AWS quota increases and sanitize traces for bench by Thu 2026-12-10. 4) Schedule benchmark start for Mon 2026-12-14. 5) Redwood to supply bench harness and a short runbook.
[09:48] Mark: sounds good. any other questions?
[09:52] Priya: one quick Q - do you support in-region HSM via customer KMS with bring-your-own-key?
[09:58] Samir: yes bring-your-own-key via KMS is supported; if you need HSM we have partners and can document the flow.
[10:06] Lena: great. thanks everyone. we'll wait for the security pack.
[10:10] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling.
[10:15] [call ended]
next_steps: Maya: send security pack and sample SOW by 2026-12-07
Rajiv (Redwood): share endpoint service name and peering runbook by 2026-12-10
Aurora: submit AWS quota requests and sanitize traces by 2026-12-10

Rajiv (Redwood deployment): create endpoint service and coordinate peering acceptance (due 2026-12-10)
Lena Ortiz: request AWS ENI and vpc peering quotas (due 2026-12-10)
Samir Patel: provide benchmarking harness and runbook (due 2026-12-13)
